--- title: beta_convergence --- ```python beta_convergence( data, variable, controls=None, *, first=None, last=None, model='ols', w=None, fixed_effects=None, vcov='hetero', draws=10000, seed=12345, min_obs=10, title=None, map=None, gdf=None, ref=None, ) ``` Beta-convergence: did the units that started lower grow faster between two years? Regresses each unit's average yearly log growth between ``first`` and ``last`` on the logarithm of its level in ``first``. A negative slope is convergence. ## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} | Name | Type | Description | Default | |---------------|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------| | data | | A dataset id, or a panel with ``geo_id`` and ``year``, e.g. from ``load`` | _required_ | | variable | str | A numeric, strictly positive column in levels (its logarithm is taken here, so do not pass a variable that is already a logarithm) | _required_ | | controls | | Numeric column(s) that enter at their value in ``first`` (conditional convergence) | `None` | | first | | The two years (default: the first and the last year with data) | `None` | | last | | The two years (default: the first and the last year with data) | `None` | | model | str | ``"ols"``, or a spatial model estimated on the boundaries' weights: ``"sar"`` (spatial lag of growth), ``"sem"`` (spatial error), ``"slx"`` (spatial lags of the regressors) or ``"sdm"`` (spatial Durbin: both lags) | `'ols'` | | w | | Spatial weights from ``weights`` for the spatial models (default: queen contiguity among the units with data in both years) | `None` | | fixed_effects | | Column(s), or coarser scale(s) the units lie in (e.g. the scale above them), that enter as dummy variables | `None` | | vcov | str | Standard errors of the OLS estimate: ``"hetero"`` (robust, HC1) or ``"iid"`` | `'hetero'` | | draws | int | Simulation draws behind the standard errors of the spatial models' impacts | `10000` | | seed | int | Makes the draws reproducible | `12345` | | min_obs | int | The fewest units the regression accepts | `10` | | title | str \| None | The figure title | `None` | | map | str \| None | The map (scale) the units are drawn on and their neighbours found, e.g. one of the project's municipal maps (default: the data's own map; needed only for a table whose units are on several maps and that does not record which, see ``geo.scales()``) | `None` | | gdf | | Boundaries to use instead of the project's (a GeoDataFrame with ``geo_id``). Boundaries are loaded only for the spatial models; with ``"ols"``, passing ``gdf`` adds the growth map | `None` | ## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns} | Name | Type | Description | |--------|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | | result object | A result with ``.beta_total`` (the slope; for the spatial models the total impact, next to ``.beta_direct`` and ``.beta_indirect``, the spillover), their standard errors ``.se_total``, ``.se_direct`` and ``.se_indirect``, ``.speed`` (of convergence, per year) and ``.half_life`` (years to close half of a gap), ``.rho`` and ``.lam`` (the spatial parameters), ``.r2``, ``.aic``, ``.n_obs``, ``.horizon`` (years between ``first`` and ``last``), ``.df`` (one row per unit: ``initial``, ``final``, ``growth`` and the controls), ``.fig`` (growth against the initial log level, with the fitted line), ``.fig_conditional`` (the same with controls and fixed effects partialled out; ``None`` without them), ``.fig_map`` (the map of growth; ``None`` without boundaries), ``.gt`` and ``.summary`` (the estimates; the OLS column is always there), ``.impacts`` (every regressor's impacts, spatial models), ``.w_spec``, ``.notes`` and ``.interpret()``. | ## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example} ```python !pip install -q geo4bolivia import geo4bolivia as geo res = geo.beta_convergence("sdg", "index_sdg") # ~2012 to ~2024 print(res.interpret()) res.fig ``` ::: {#cf121d30 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} Across 343 units, the growth of **Sustainable Development Index, IDS (0-100)** over a 12-year window is associated with its initial log level with a total slope of **-0.0287** (SE 0.00171), statistically significant at the 1% level. The slope is negative — the β-convergence pattern: units that started lower tended to grow faster, narrowing initial gaps. That slope implies a convergence speed of λ = 0.0351 per year and a half-life of about 19.7 years — the time for half of an initial gap to close at this pace. _These are associations, not causal effects. A causal reading needs a research design._ ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: :::
